questions.name: decision
questions.question: You are the inventory planner of this store. Decide what to do with this product today. Low stock alone does NOT mean reorder: weigh the demand trend, customers already waiting, incoming stock, supplier lead time and reliability, the minimum order size, the risk of excess inventory and any anomaly in the sales data.

options.label: REORDER
options.definition: Place a normal replenishment order now: stock will run out around or before a new order could arrive, demand is healthy, and the order will not leave excessive inventory.

options.label: PRIORITIZE
options.definition: Urgent replenishment that must be handled first today: customers are already waiting or a stockout is imminent or already happening while demand is real, so waiting would lose sales or customers.

options.label: WAIT
options.definition: Do not order now: available plus incoming stock covers demand until a later order could arrive, or demand is falling so an order would likely create excess stock.

options.label: ALERT
options.definition: No purchase, but a person should look at it: excess inventory tying up money, or abnormal sales behaviour while stock is available (for example sales suddenly stopped).

options.label: HUMAN_REVIEW
options.definition: Ambiguous or high-risk: signals conflict, demand may be a one-off spike or a data error, or an expensive order would rest on uncertain demand. A person must decide before buying.

options.label: critical

questions.question: Will this product be unable to serve customers before a new order placed today could arrive (considering customers already waiting and incoming units)?

questions.name: real_demand_growth
questions.question: Is genuine customer demand for this product growing, and not just a one-off spike, a data error or an effect of being out of stock?

questions.name: overstock_risk
questions.question: If the store placed the order described in planning_math_by_n8n today, would it likely end up with excess inventory (well over 60 days of sales) or money tied up in slow stock?
